Method.evidence: Class868s reply dispatcher 0x06000C7D switches on the ResultCode (values now read with --dump-constants: E_SUCCESS 0, E_SUCCESS_WITH_CRC 1, E_BUSY_TIMEOUT 2, E_BUSY 3, E_SESSION_REFUSED 225, E_NO_SESSION_ACTIVE 226, E_SUBSERVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED 227, E_DATA_VOID 248, E_ERROR 255) and on PollCycleState (Idle 0, Polling 1, TimerExpiredPerformLastTry 2), and reading it with instruction offsets (new perf-now/iloff.py) attributes every call to its case. Four actions are length checks through the already named Class823::VerifyLengthEqualTo - exactly 3 bytes for a success reply, 4 for Data Void in Idle without a retry, 3 for Busy in Polling, 5 for Busy Timeout in Polling - and five throw an ApplicationLayerException: e for E_ERROR, d for E_SESSION_REFUSED, c for E_NO_SESSION_ACTIVE, b for E_SUBSERVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED (all with the unresolvable error, cannot process the state/return code text) and a for a busy/timeout reply that arrives while the cycle is not Polling with the retry flag set, whose own text is return code {0} : unresolvable MaC error, cannot process the return code.
Method.themes: New helper perf-now/iloff.py prints offset-annotated IL (from --inspect-methods) so a switch table maps to the calls it selects - the missing half of dispatch-map.py, which prints branch targets without the offsets of the instructions that carry them. This closed the last Class868 block: with the constants, the offsets and the already named VerifyLengthEqualTo, all nine actions were decidable.
